overview: New Hope Corporation is an Australian thermal coal producer headquartered in Brisbane, operating the wholly-owned New Acland open-cut mine in Queensland, an 80% joint-venture interest in the Bengalla open-cut mine in New South Wales, and a 25.97% equity interest in Malabar Resources (owner of the Maxwell underground mine). The Group also owns the Queensland Bulk Handling coal export terminal at the Port of Brisbane and runs pastoral/agricultural operations on land associated with its mining tenements. Coal is sold predominantly into Asian seaborne markets (Japan, China, South Korea, Taiwan) with a small domestic component, and the company has exited non-core oil and gas (divested Bridgeport Energy in September 2025) to focus exclusively on low-cost, long-life coal assets.

business_model.summary: New Hope generates revenue almost entirely from mining and selling thermal (energy) coal FOB into seaborne export markets, indexed broadly to benchmark prices (Newcastle gC NEWC 6000 and API-5 5500). Revenue is transactional/commodity-price-driven rather than recurring or contracted, with realized prices moving with global thermal coal indices, FX and product quality (ash/CV blend). A minority of earnings comes from the equity-accounted Malabar Resources stake (Maxwell underground metallurgical/thermal mine) and from third-party throughput and agricultural (pastoral) operations, both immaterial to group economics.

revenue_streams.name: New Acland Mine (100% owned, thermal coal, ramping to 5Mtpa)
Queensland Bulk Handling (port throughput, incl. 3rd party)
Malabar Resources equity interest (Maxwell Mine, equity-accounted, not consolidated revenue)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - global utilities, traders and industrial coal buyers; ~91% of FY26 coal sales into Asia (China 26%, Japan 37%, Korea 22%, Taiwan 1%, other Asia ~5%), ~7% domestic NSW/QLD
business_model.geographic_mix: Mining operations 100% Australia (Queensland - New Acland; New South Wales - Bengalla, Maxwell); sales revenue ~91% export (Asia), ~9% domestic/other

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier Australian thermal coal producer (~11.5Mt saleable FY26 on 80%-Bengalla basis); smaller and more thermal-pure than Whitehaven (which has pivoted toward metallurgical coal via Blackwater/Daunia) and Yancoal; a price-taker in a global seaborne market with no pricing power over benchmark indices

moat_factors.description: Bengalla and New Acland are described by management as low-cost, long-life mines with approvals into the 2030s and FOB cash costs (~$89/t FY26) that provide margin resilience versus higher-cost global thermal coal supply, though this is a relative cost advantage, not a structural moat
Wholly-owned port terminal at Port of Brisbane (leases to 2042) secures export logistics and offers some optionality via third-party throughput fees, reducing reliance on third-party port allocation

Existing mining leases and approvals are a barrier to new thermal coal entrants in Australia given the difficulty of obtaining new coal project approvals; New Acland Stage 3's decade-long approval fight illustrates how hard it now is for a new entrant to replicate
Net cash position of ~$482m (FY26) plus ~$778m total liquidity provides resilience through commodity cycles and funds growth capex without dilution

weaknesses: Pure commodity price-taker with no ability to influence global thermal coal prices
Single-commodity concentration (thermal coal) with no diversification into higher-value metallurgical coal (unlike Whitehaven/Yancoal)

Geographic production concentration in two Australian coal basins, exposed to weather (wet-weather pit disruption at Bengalla in FY25), rail/port logistics constraints, and Queensland/NSW-specific regulatory risk
High-ash/lower-CV product mix at times depresses realized pricing relative to benchmark indices

New Acland Mine has a multi-decade history of legal and regulatory challenges (Oakey Coal Action Alliance litigation, Land Court proceedings) illustrating elevated approval/execution risk for expansion

growth_drivers: New Acland Mine ramp-up toward 5Mtpa target, with Manning Vale West pit access expected Q4 calendar 2026 unlocking further production growth (FY27 guidance ~4Mt, FY28 ~4.5-4.6Mt at New Acland)
Bengalla Mine sustained at 13.4Mtpa ROM (100% basis) run-rate following FY25 weather-related disruption recovery
Group FY27 indicative saleable coal production guidance of ~12.7Mt (excluding Maxwell), implying continued organic volume growth

Increasing equity stake in Malabar Resources (now 25.97%) providing indirect exposure to the newly commissioned Maxwell Underground Mine (first longwall coal April 2026, officially opened July 2026), diversifying earnings into a higher-priced coal product (7% premium to gC NEWC 6000)
Queensland Government's October 2025 decision removing the New Acland Stage 3 rail loop condition, reducing capital and approval friction for the mine's growth path
Disciplined capital management and capital returns (dividends, DRP, ongoing $100m buy-back authorization) supported by a significant franking credit balance
Structural thermal coal supply tightness thesis: management and some analysts cite under-investment in new global thermal coal supply and ageing mines supporting medium-term pricing

business.description: Group earnings are almost entirely leveraged to thermal coal prices and volumes with minimal diversification; FY26 underlying EBITDA fell 33% and NPAT fell 63% predominantly on lower realized pricing and higher unit costs
Rail performance impacted by Cross River Rail possession outages, Queensland Rail industrial action and network disruptions in FY26; weather events disrupted Bengalla in FY25
FOB cash costs rose 7.9% in FY26 driven by higher strip ratio at Bengalla and elevated diesel prices linked to Middle East conflict
Continued dependence on completing the Manning Vale West road realignment and pit access on schedule to reach 5Mtpa; history of delays at this asset

financial.description: Realized AUD sales prices are affected by USD-referenced coal indices and AUD/USD movements; FY26 pricing was hurt by unfavourable FX
Issued $300m new convertible notes due 2032 (2.625% coupon) while repurchasing 97.77% of 2029 notes; capped call transactions partially hedge dilution but conversion risk remains
Large franking credit balance and disciplined capital return framework somewhat mitigate risk, but growth capex requirements and equity stake purchases (Malabar) compete with shareholder returns

regulatory.description: New Acland Stage 3 has a long history of Land Court challenges and community opposition (Oakey Coal Action Alliance); while major approvals and the rail loop condition removal were resolved by late 2025, further conditions (road realignment, community funding) and ongoing regulatory engagement remain

FY26 marks first year of mandatory AASB S2 climate-related financial disclosures; increasing scrutiny on Scope 1-3 emissions, transition planning and potential future carbon costs or environmental bonding requirements
Queensland and NSW coal royalty rates are a direct cost lever for state governments; FY26 royalties paid were $164.7m with an effective tax rate of 36.5%, above the statutory 30% corporate rate

macro.description: Newcastle (gC NEWC 6000) and API-5 index prices are volatile and driven by global energy demand, LNG availability, Chinese import/domestic production dynamics, and weather; FY26 saw softening H1 prices followed by H2 strength from Middle East conflict-driven gas-to-coal switching

Structural, long-term shift away from thermal coal in power generation as renewables and gas substitute; despite near-term IEA demand upgrades, the secular trajectory for seaborne thermal coal is widely expected to decline, pressuring long-run asset values and access to capital/insurance
Diesel price exposure (up 21.7% in FY26 on Middle East conflict) directly affects FOB cash costs; broader mining input cost inflation (labour, equipment, explosives)
Increasing reluctance among banks, insurers and some investors to finance or underwrite thermal coal assets could raise New Hope's cost of capital or restrict access to capital markets over time

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global seaborne thermal coal trade remains large (~900Mt+ annually) but faces a structurally challenged long-term growth outlook amid the global energy transition; near-term dynamics are more constructive, with the IEA revising 2026 global coal demand upward (+1.2% to ~8.94 billion tonnes) on gas-to-coal switching amid elevated LNG prices, and thermal coal indices recovering from 2025 lows (Newcastle averaged US$119.7/t in FY26, up modestly YoY) supported by geopolitical disruption and Chinese demand
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - thermal coal is a highly cyclical commodity business; NHC's earnings swing materially with benchmark index prices (FY26 underlying EBITDA fell 33% even as volumes grew, illustrating price sensitivity dominating volume growth)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct sensitivity given net cash balance sheet (~$482m net cash FY26) and low leverage; indirect sensitivity via global growth/energy demand and AUD/USD exchange rate movements that affect discount rates on future mine value and equity valuations

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results released: revenue $1,766.5m (down 0.5%), underlying EBITDA $514.3m (down 32.8%), NPAT $161.0m (down 63.4%), full-year dividend raised to 40 cents/share fully franked (FY25: 34 cents) despite the earnings decline; shares rose ~3.5% to near 52-week highs on the print

Analyst consensus rating 'Hold' with average 12-month price target around $5.34, below the prevailing share price near $6.47, implying analysts see the stock as fully to richly valued after the FY26 rally

Completed issuance of $300m senior unsecured convertible notes due 2032 (2.625% fixed coupon) and repurchased 97.77% of existing 2029 convertible notes, extending debt maturity profile and reducing near-term refinancing risk; notes listed on SGX-ST

Malabar Resources officially opened the Maxwell Underground Mine (25.97%-owned by New Hope), marking transition from construction to production and supporting 430 permanent jobs; first longwall coal was cut 14 April 2026

Queensland Government Coordinator-General removed the New Acland Stage 3 dedicated rail loop condition, replacing it with revised road infrastructure and community funding commitments, reducing land disturbance by ~100 hectares and simplifying the path to full Stage 3 production

Completed divestment of Bridgeport Energy Pty Ltd (oil and gas), exiting the sector entirely to focus on core coal operations; net cash outflow of $12.1m plus contingent working-capital/bonding facilities provided to the buyer
Malabar Resources (NHC's 25.97%-owned associate) executed a US$330m senior debt facility to refinance existing debt and provide additional liquidity for Maxwell Mine ramp-up

items.notes: Indicative guidance excluding the 25.97% interest in Maxwell Mine; implies continued organic growth from FY26's 11.5Mt actual

Ramp toward 5Mtpa target expected within ~18 months of Manning Vale West pit access (scheduled Q4 CY2026); management flagged conservatism given rail risk (Cross River Rail delays, Queensland Rail industrial action)
Expected to continue at the targeted run-rate following FY26 recovery from FY25 weather disruption

items.metric: New Acland Stage 3 road works capex
items.notes: Supports mine growth; remaining approval-related public road realignment works to be completed progressively as mining advances

items.target: Return to a 'more sustainable level' of capex
items.notes: FY26 capex of $185.2m was already 37.4% below FY25 ($295.7m) as the Bengalla Growth Project completed; further moderation expected as New Acland growth capital (fleet, Manning Vale West) is substantially committed

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Robert Millner and CEO Robert Bishop both reiterated confidence in medium-to-long-term thermal coal price support, citing a global supply shortfall from ageing assets and underinvestment in new projects. Management stated the Group is 'transitioning out of our capital investment period in the coming years' and expects the organic growth pipeline (Manning Vale West, Bengalla sustaining, Malabar/Maxwell ramp-up) to provide 'significant upside to future cash flows for investors' with a continued focus on shareholder returns, noting the Group's significant franking credit balance and an active but currently unused $100m on-market buy-back authorization.

bull_case: Strong balance sheet with ~$482m net cash and ~$778m total liquidity gives resilience through commodity down-cycles and funds growth without needing dilutive equity raises

Multi-year organic production growth pipeline (New Acland to 5Mtpa, Bengalla at 13.4Mtpa run-rate, Malabar/Maxwell ramp-up) is now substantially funded, positioning the Group for volume-driven earnings growth as capex intensity declines

Regulatory overhang at New Acland has substantially cleared (Stage 3 rail loop condition removed, Land Court/OCAA litigation resolved), reducing a long-standing execution risk that previously delayed the asset for years

High and growing fully franked dividend (40 cents FY26, up from 34 cents FY25) backed by significant franking credits and management's explicit focus on shareholder returns, appealing to income-focused investors

Thermal coal prices have shown resilience/upside surprise (Middle East-driven gas-to-coal switching, Chinese import demand, IEA upgraded 2026 demand forecast), providing near-term earnings support despite the longer-term decarbonization narrative
bear_case: Pure-play thermal coal exposure faces a structural, long-term secular decline as the global energy system decarbonizes, raising questions about terminal asset values, financing/insurance access and eventual multiple compression

Earnings are highly cyclical and price-taking; FY26 showed how quickly a modest volume increase can be overwhelmed by lower realized pricing and higher unit costs, with underlying EBITDA down 33% and NPAT down 63% year-on-year

Analyst consensus (average price target ~$5.34, 'Hold' rating) sits well below the recent share price (~$6.47 post-results), suggesting the stock may already price in optimistic production growth and coal price assumptions

New Acland's history of prolonged legal and regulatory challenges illustrates the execution risk inherent in Australian coal project approvals; further conditions, community opposition or rail/logistics constraints (already disrupted FY26 sales) could delay the ramp to 5Mtpa

Concentrated in two ageing coal basins with rising strip ratios (Bengalla FY26 strip ratio 5.1x vs 4.6x) and cost inflation (FOB cash costs up 7.9% in FY26), which could erode the low-cost advantage that underpins the investment thesis over time
